messages.subject: Standard Error Calculations
parts:
Hi!

I am attempting to calculate standard errors for my parameters in a three factor model with 209 variables and 56 groups (so a large model). However, even when the max changes is small (0.0002), I cannot get models to save if I have set SE=TRUE.  After so many iterations, it will just say "Calculating information matrix..." and nothing will change for 24 hrs. I am using mirtCluster() and different SE.types (I've tried SEM and crossprod) to try and improve the speed, but I haven't had any luck. 

I also tried boot.mirt(); however, I got a warning that SE are not meaningful for slope parameters in explanatory models. I'm confused why these SEs would be different than the ones in the model. 

Any thoughts on how to get around this?

My model script is below!

Thank you, 
Leigh 

Grouped_MIRT_Model<- multipleGroup(Individual_MIRTData_test[,c(3:211)], 
                                               model = 3,
                                               group = as.character(Individual_MIRTData_test$V2.x),
                                               rotate = "none",
                                               invariance = c("slopes","intercepts","free_means"),
                                               itemtype=itemT,
                                               method = "EM", SE=TRUE, SE.type="crossprod",
                           technical=list(NCYCLES=30), pars=Parameters,
                                               survey.weights = Individual_MIRTData_test$V258.x,
                                               large=Large)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Standard Error Calculations
parts:
56 groups! I can't say I've tested mirt before with that many groups. It's possible this is just a *really* difficult estimation problem, so the ACOV is getting bogged down in all the maths. If you'd like, I could try to reproduce the problem to see if something internally is getting hung up, but in all honesty this could just be a bottle neck of the mirt software.

Phil
